brief: A cheat sheet for Ubuntu CLI commands, formatted nicely in slides for easy reference. It should include common commands, usage examples, and any relevant tips.

spec.title: Ubuntu CLI Cheat Sheet
spec.subtitle: Essential Commands for Efficiency and Control
spec.author: System Administrator

slides.title: Ubuntu CLI Cheat Sheet
slides.subtitle: Essential Commands for Efficiency and Control
slides.notes: Introduction to the presentation. Frame this as a navigational tool for the shell environment.

slides.title: Navigating the File System
bullets: pwd: Display the current working directory path
ls -la: List all files and directories with details
cd [directory]: Change directory to the specified path
mkdir [name]: Create a new directory
rmdir [name]: Remove an empty directory
slides.notes: Start with basics. These commands form the foundation of file system interaction.

slides.title: File Operations

left.title: Management
bullets: touch [file]: Create an empty file
cp [source] [dest]: Copy files or directories
mv [source] [dest]: Move or rename files

right.title: Removal & Viewing
bullets: rm [file]: Remove a specific file
rm -rf [dir]: Remove a directory and contents
cat [file]: Display entire file content
less [file]: View file content with paging

slides.notes: Warn about the 'rm -rf' command, as it is destructive and requires caution.

slides.title: Permissions & Ownership
slides.body: Control access to your files and directories with these utilities.
bullets: chmod [mode] [file]: Change file access permissions
chown [user]:[group] [file]: Change file ownership
sudo [command]: Execute a command as superuser
slides.notes: Emphasize that chmod and chown are critical for security administration.

slides.title: Package Management
slides.notes: Walk through the logical workflow of keeping a system up to date.

slides.title: System Monitoring
bullets: top: Real-time system resource monitor
htop: Interactive process viewer (installable)
df -h: Check disk space usage in human-readable format
free -m: View memory usage in megabytes
uptime: Display system uptime and load average
slides.notes: Focus on diagnostic commands used for troubleshooting system performance.

slides.title: Network Utilities

left.title: Connectivity
bullets: ping [host]: Test network connectivity
ip addr: Display network interface IP addresses
curl [url]: Transfer data from or to a server

right.title: Secure Access
bullets: ssh [user]@[host]: Secure remote login
scp [file] [user]@[host]: Secure copy files
ufw status: Check firewall status

slides.notes: These are essential for remote server management and basic debugging.

slides.title: Text Processing Shortcuts
bullets: grep '[pattern]' [file]: Search for text in a file
head -n [num] [file]: View the first few lines of a file
tail -f [file]: Monitor file changes in real-time
history: View previously executed commands
slides.notes: Highlight 'tail -f' as essential for reading log files dynamically.

slides.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
bullets: Ctrl + C: Kill the current foreground process
Ctrl + Z: Suspend the current process
Ctrl + A / E: Move cursor to start or end of line
Tab: Autocomplete file names and commands
Clear: Clear the terminal screen
slides.notes: These shortcuts significantly increase terminal speed and quality of life.

slides.title: Mastering the Terminal
slides.subtitle: Practice leads to proficiency
bullets: Always verify critical commands before execution
Utilize 'man [command]' for detailed manuals
Create aliases for frequently used complex strings
slides.notes: Encourage the user to read 'man' pages, as they are the primary documentation source.

spec.notesForUser: No placeholders were needed. Ensure the audience is aware that sudo usage requires administrative privileges.
